_comment: 🛑🛑 DO NOT APPLY THIS FILE YET. 🛑🛑
S3 bucket policy ADDITION — agrisync-raw-ap-south-1. PHASE 2 of the
raw-bucket encryption rail. Authored per §11's 'Only then add the deny
rail' step — authored because §11 asks for it, NOT presented as safe to
apply. This is explicitly out of this lane's scope to sequence or land;
it is captured here so the shape exists and the ordering hazard is
impossible to miss.
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
MANDATORY ORDER, PER §11 ('Raw bucket — and the order within this task is
mandatory'): 1. Unswallow the failure first (log with the CONFIGURED
bucket name, not the hardcoded RawBlobStoreOptions.BucketName default that
can lie about what's actually being written to; add a metric + alarm).
2. THEN bind an explicit RawBlobStore section in production config and
change its .Bind() to ValidateOnStart, so a missing section is a boot
failure, not a silent fallback to the hardcoded default. 3. ONLY THEN add
this deny rail. All three of those are src/ changes (Program.cs,
RawBlobStoreOptions.cs, appsettings.Production.json, S3RawBlobStore.cs) —
out of this lane's allowlist (aws/, .github/, .husky/ only) and explicitly
flagged as another agent's work in this lane's task brief.
WHY THE ORDER IS MANDATORY, STATED PLAINLY: if this policy is applied
while RawBlobStoreOptions.KmsKeyId is still unbound/null in production,
S3RawBlobStore.PutAsync (src/apps/ShramSafal/ShramSafal.Infrastructure/
Storage/S3RawBlobStore.cs) falls back to plain AES256 SSE (see its
'nullable KmsKeyId ... falls back to AES256' comment) — and this policy
would then deny EVERY PutObject for lacking the required KMS key header.
Verified live 2026-08-15 (read-only): no KMS alias containing 'raw'
exists in this account yet (aws kms list-aliases), so as of today the key
genuinely is unbound — applying this file today would fail 100% of raw-
blob writes immediately.
AND — per this plan section's own read-path warning — the write path that
calls PutAsync swallows the resulting exception. The caller would not see
an error; the farmer's app would show success (HTTP 200) while the voice
clip or receipt evidence silently never reached durable storage. This is
the exact failure class the whole architecture migration exists to end.
Do not apply this file until the unswallow + bind steps above are
confirmed live in production, independently of this bucket-policy change.
ONCE THE CMK EXISTS AND RawBlobStoreOptions IS BOUND to it in prod:
1. Replace <RAW_BLOB_CMK_ARN> below with the real key ARN (not an alias —
the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id condition value
AWS returns on PutObject is the full key ARN, not the alias).
2. Merge this Statement array into bucket-policy.json's Statement array
(do not apply as a second separate put-bucket-policy call — that
replaces the whole policy document and would silently drop the
Phase 1 TLS/encryption-header statements).
3. Re-encrypt the 41 existing objects in place (§11: 'Re-encrypt the 41
existing objects in place afterwards') — a separate, explicit
re-encryption pass; this policy does not retroactively re-encrypt
anything already written under AES256.
4. Apply via aws/raw/apply-config.sh as ONE transaction with the rest of
bucket-policy.json, per the 'ONE desired-state transaction per
bucket' rule — not as a fourth ad-hoc put-bucket-policy call.
D9 note: this statement changes WHICH KEY encrypts new writes. It does
not add, remove, or shorten any expiration/transition/deletion action —
no D9 conflict. Retention is governed entirely by lifecycle-policy.json
(which contains none of those actions on this bucket), not by this file.
